text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions flat-topped and flesh-colored with a central dimple? Do they appear to be spreading in linear clusters along scratch marks?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those features are classic for Molluscum contagiosum, a viral infection common in young children. Given the daycare exposure and the specific appearance of the lesions, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
